claim: Ratchet violations are read from the merged output: run_child returns stdout then stderr in one string, so a warning on stderr becomes a new violation on every run.
The baseline is read from the check copy after the command ran; a guard that rewrites its own baseline (rubocop --auto-gen-config, tee) passes every violation.
Output cut at MAX_OUTPUT (16 MiB) or by the 2 s pipe drain makes missing lines look fixed, and tightening deletes real baseline lines.
Path::components drops inner `.` and empty components, so `a/./b` and `a//b` would load although AC-1 and AC-2 refuse `.`; the check must split the string at `/`.
Committing a tightened baseline moves HEAD past the passing check record; no criterion says whether the close needs another full check, and the AC-10 line does not ask for the commit.
Guards rely on the lazy checkout of Runner::project; with no project commands, or after a project command that edits files, guards may run in a stale or dirty copy.
A dir such as tests or src passes the lexical check, so every builder write under it is denied and every main-agent edit asks; refuse or warn about a dir that overlaps source or test folders.
The record test of step 3 has only exit-code guards; nonzero new and removed counts of ratchet guards are tested nowhere.
